$comment: What 'the index works' means, in a file rather than in someone's memory. `bbgraph.py selftest` runs it and exits non-zero on any mismatch. Expectations are about the leading MODULE for code questions, because that is the file an agent opens. When a source change legitimately moves an answer, update the expectation in the same commit and say why -- an unexplained edit here is how a ranking bug gets ratified.

queries.note: Regression guard for structural rank deciding rather than ordering. `protocol` is reached by 28 of 33 modules; with an unconditional load-bearing multiplier it won this query outright, which is the download-count failure the method exists to avoid.
None of these three words is a module name; this passes on module doc-comment vocabulary.
Compound-name lookup. Returned `presentation` while a name match required the whole underscored string to appear as one query token.
Not history_store: the store is the persistence layer, the history is the object.

no_match.note: Must return nothing rather than dress a guess as a ranking.

confidence.note: Right answer, low confidence, and that is correct. No subsystem matched this wording, so the ranking is term overlap. Weak-but-right and weak-and-wrong are not separable here, and answering nonsense confidently is the worse failure.
Out of scope. One token lands on host heap metrics; a partial match is not confidence in the query.

$counts_comment: schemas counts PROTOCOL SURFACE only. 23 further schema strings are declared inside a #[cfg(test)] mod and are fixtures; counting them reported 81/50, overstating both the surface and the gap. The boundary is the mod, not the attribute: keying on the first #[cfg(test)] line demoted history.rs GENESIS_SCHEMA and RECEIPT_SCHEMA, both pub, because two test-only use lines sit above them. `bitblock/test-object/v1` is the clearest case -- frame.rs and storage.rs each coined it independently in their own tests, and it had been fusing them into a shared subsystem. schemas_vectored moved 42 -> 44 when journal/rejected-tail/v1 and storage-record/envelope/v1 gained independent Python suites; they were the only two protocol objects with no vector and no literal tag assertion.

structure.note: The most load-bearing module in the workspace. Gained one dependent when the crate split introduced src/lib.rs as a facade that re-exports it -- a re-export is a real edge. Was 28 while the dep scan matched only `crate::` and missed the binary's `bitblock::` imports.

Two thirds of the crate reaches the world model, most of it through frame and render rather than directly. Counted over production scope only: 31 of 145 dependency edges were `use crate::x` inside `mod tests`, which is a real import but not a coupling that constrains where shared code may live.
A leaf: research-only, nothing depends on it. Safe to change in isolation.

schemas.note: The canonical framebuffer domain. An independent Python reconstruction must keep agreeing with it.

Recorded as uncovered on purpose. 16 of 58 protocol objects have no independent vectors, and pretending otherwise would make the coverage number meaningless. If someone writes vectors for this, flip it here in the same commit.
Was one of the two objects nothing independently checked. The vector varies offset and suffix separately, because the tag exists to bind both.

The outermost envelope. Its vector rebuilds magic, version, declared length, parent flag, kind name, object digest, schema and payload, and both sides assert the same literal record tag over the `on 0 0 0` edit from edit_vectors.py.

$reuse_comment: Compression targets, so a refactor that claims to remove duplication has to move these. Production and test scope are separate on purpose: the first pass measured them together and named presentation_output <-> _v2 the biggest target in the crate, when most of that pair's overlap is test fixtures. Numbers here are the measured baseline, not a goal - the tree turned out to be far less duplicated than the first scan suggested.
